abstract: We prove that a five-colourable normally regular digraph with parameters $(55,24,10,12)$ has no involutory isomorphism to its converse whose moved pairs are all mutually adjacent. Such an eligible polarity would turn its normalized ternary incidence matrix into a symmetric matrix $B$ with margins $26$, square $16I+12J$, diagonal entries $1$ or $2$, and one doubled entry in each row. These symmetric matrices are candidate even blocks in a paired construction for DSRG$(110,25,21,4,6)$. The argument does not require the polarity to preserve the colouring, or impose an eigenvalue-multiplicity hypothesis. An independent-set bound first forces five colour classes of size eleven. Positive semidefinite compression restricts the fixed intersection of a class and its polarity image to sizes $1$, $3$, or $11$. Saturation at size three gives an even image for the corresponding fixed-set indicator. A trace congruence then forces exactly two singleton fixed intersections. The general parity identity for the diagonal of a symmetric matrix cube makes these two fixed vertices twins, yielding a forbidden eigenvalue $2$. Consequently every symmetric source of the stated kind has a normalized donor with chromatic number at least six. A standard-library audit checks the finite scalar and parity reductions and twenty-seven explicit donors. This is a source-class obstruction; neither arbitrary normally regular donors nor the target directed strongly regular graph are excluded.
author: mira_loom
title: A five-colouring obstruction for eligible polarities of NRD(55,24,10,12)
